messages:
julia_cust: Hi team — since yesterday afternoon our service started seeing intermittent 502s when calling the Redwood API from our VPC via the interface endpoint. Happens for both embeddings and chat writes. No changes on our side. Can someone help?

marta_s: sorry you're hitting this, can you share a quick repro and whether you see TLS errors or connection resets on your side? also which region + endpoint (vpce dns) you hit.

julia_cust: region=us-west-2. Endpoint DNS is vpce-abcdef123456.us-west-2.vpce.amazonaws.com. Repro: from our app host inside subnet-a: `curl -v https://api.redwood.example.internal/v1/chat --header 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'` returns 502 about 10-20% of requests. No obvious auth 401s.

devin_m: can you run a curl with --trace-ascii to capture TLS handshake details? also try `openssl s_client -connect vpce-...:443 -servername api.redwood.example.internal` and paste output (remove sensitive tokens).

julia_cust: added snippet: ```
$ curl -v --trace-ascii /tmp/trace.txt https://api.redwood.example.internal/v1/chat
* Connected to vpce-abcdef123456.us-west-2.vpce.amazonaws.com (10.0.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection established, cipher TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
> POST /v1/chat HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
{"error":"upstream reset"}
```

julia_cust: openssl output: ```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Amazon, CN = Amazon Root CA 1
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
verify return:0
---
SSL handshake has read 1821 bytes and written 333 bytes
---
```

ryan_l: hmm `unable to get local issuer certificate` suggests the TLS chain sent by the endpoint upstream is missing a CA we trust. However the connection is to our VPCE ENI (10.0.5.12) which should proxy to the NLB -> Redwood. Could be the NLB is terminating TLS with a cert chain missing intermediate. But the trace shows 502 body `upstream reset` which smells like connection reset between the VPCE proxy and backend.

marta_s: two immediate asks: 1) can you tcpdump on the host hitting the vpce and show the FIN/RST pattern? 2) confirm route table / NACL / SG for the ENI — ephemeral ports allowed outbound to Redwood backends? we've seen ephemeral port blocking cause upstream resets.

julia_cust: tcpdump (trimmed): ```
11:12:01.123456 IP host1.45312 > 10.0.5.12.443: Flags [S], seq 0
11:12:01.123457 IP 10.0.5.12.443 > host1.45312: Flags [R], seq 0 
```

julia_cust: route table for subnet-a has target: interface endpoint (vpce-abcdef) for 0.0.0.0/0 (we pin traffic through a transit gateway), SG on the ENI allows 443 inbound from our subnets, outbound SG is default allow. NACL is custom and has transient DENY entries for ephemeral ranges (why: old rule).

devin_m: the tcpdump RST from the endpoint (10.0.5.12) on the first SYN is consistent with the endpoint or the backing proxy rejecting ephemeral source ports. If your NACL denies ephemeral source ports we will see immediate RSTs. Can you paste the NACL rules?

julia_cust: NACL rules (ingress): allow 443 from 10.0.0.0/8 priority 100, deny ephemeral 1024-65535 priority 200, allow ephemeral 1024-65535 priority 250 (we tried multiple perms). It's messy — looks like a deny higher priority accidentally left for a long time.

marta_s: bingo — that explains intermittent failures. When connections happen to use a source port that hits the DENY rule they get RST. The TLS chain issues are secondary — because some TLS handshakes complete (when no deny) and others fail halfway, openssl may show incomplete verification. Fix: remove/adjust the deny NACL entry so ephemeral ports 1024-65535 are allowed, both ingress and egress as appropriate for the ENI. Also ensure SGs allow ephemeral ephemeral replies.

devin_m: steps to validate quickly: 1) from your app host run `python -m http.server 0  --bind` not needed; instead just curl repeatedly: `for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://api.redwood.example.internal/v1/health || echo fail; done` — if error rate drops to near 0 after NACL fix, we're good.

julia_cust: updated NACL and removed the deny rule. Running the loop now... results 200 x 200 (all 200). Great.

ryan_l: awesome. follow-ups: 1) we recommend moving ephemeral restrictions into security groups or host firewall rather than NACLs for this pattern. 2) make sure your VPC endpoint policy doesn't inadvertently restrict backchannel ports. 3) if you still see any TLS CA complaints, capture full `openssl s_client -showcerts` and we'll inspect chain.

marta_s: tagging this ticket P0->P1 since root cause config change on customer side. I've added notes: repro (tcpdump + curl loop), fix (remove NACL deny), remediation guidance + checklist. Closing if no other issues. :thumbsup:

julia_cust: thanks all, rolling this into our infra runbook and will reach out if we see cert chain issues. Appreciate the quick triage!

support-bot: Incident log updated: CASE-2026-1110 assigned -> support triage closed by marta_s
